name: Evening Initiate (Piety)
body:
Note Piety feats are intended for divine-classed followers of a specific deity. Each piety feat indicates which deity in question you must have selected as your patron deity. You cannot retrain or swap out a piety feat by any means, except as described below. Should you no longer meet any of the prerequisites of a piety feat, you lose all benefits of that piety feat (including spells added to your spell list or feat(s) gained from the piety feat). If you have lost access to a piety feat in this manner, you can either seek atonement (as determined by a powerful outsider sent by your deity) to regain the benefits and use of your piety feat or you may retrain it out for another feat that you meet the prerequisites for.

However, if you wish to retrain out a defunct and inaccessible piety feat for another piety feat granted by a new patron deity, you must wait at least 30 days and prove your worth (as determined by the GM) to the church of your new patron deity before you can select the piety feat associated with that deity.

You can possess multiple piety feats if they have the same specific patron deity listed in their prerequisites; otherwise, you cannot have more than one piety feat.

Prerequisite(s): 3 class levels in any one divine spellcasting class, spellcasting ability score 15+ for that divine spellcasting class, Deific Obedience [this god], and Weapon Focus (longsword or starknife); you must have [this god] as your patron deity and your alignment must not be LG (or must be within the alignment restriction of your divine spellcasting class that requires a patron deity).

Benefit: You add Stealth and Survival as class skills. If you already have Stealth or Survival as class skill, you instead gain the Skill Focus feat for that skill as a bonus feat (you only gain one Skill Focus feat in this way). If you already have Skill Focus for both the Stealth and Survival skills when you gain this piety feat, you instead gain any one other feat as a bonus feat that you qualify for at the time you gained this piety feat. Most worshippers of [this god] typically select a combat feat in this manner.

You also add the spells below at the spell level listed to the spell list of any and all divine spellcasting classes you possess that meet the prerequisites of this piety feat.

Adding these spells as spells known does not count against your spells known limit for any such divine spellcasting classes in this manner. If you possess either the trickery or war domain, these spells are also considered domain spells for the trickery and war domains.

1st-dueling companions, fallback strategy; 2nd-flight of stars; 3rd–fractions of heal and harm; 4th-shadowy form, shadow demon aspect; 5th–covetous aura; blanket of stars

* This functions as shadow dragon aspect spell, except the appearance of the shadow form resembles a tall, four-armed humanoid with starlit feathery wings.
